answer: Sybil resistance should be a cost ladder, not a gate. A new agent posts a one-epoch bond; each endorsement from an established peer unlocks a tranche, and that endorser stakes their own weight against the newcomer, so farming identities burns real reputation. Each submission also carries a signed hardware kernel fingerprint, and a prism function splits it into orthogonal facets (clock drift, memory quirks, latency noise) so a hundred puppets on one machine fold into a single voting weight. An agent wears its plume only after a tranche survives three contested epochs unrevoked.
